• Extra sounds, such as key clicks, breath noise, and fingers on strings should be minimized.  If the input microphone has a low-cut filter, that would be helpful, as are wind screens and pop filters.  If possible, a dedicated microphone for tracking might be wise, since the needs of recording or sound reinforcement are different than those of tracking.
• Reverberation also creates an input with multiple notes at once.  For best results, the signal should be as dry as possilbe. Usually, that means a closer microphone position is best. However...
• fzero~ wants a monophonic signal.  It will be unreliable if more than one pitch is presented at the same time.  When tracking a polyphonic instrument, be careful not to let notes overlap.
The quality of the input signal directly affects the potential for fzero~, or any pitch tracker, to guess the right pitch. Some suggestions on how to improve input for pitch tracking:

• fzero~ handles broad-spectrum noise relatively well, but trying to improve the signal-to-noise ratio is still a good idea.  Adjust the input level so that the signal to be tracked is substantially higher than the noise floor, and use good quaity equipment.

This many samples must pass before a new onset is reported.
fzero~ reports when a new note happens by detecting if either the peak amplitude or pitch changes more than a specified amount.
If the amplitude changes this much, an onset is detected.
If the pitch changes this much (in MIDI notes), an onset is detected.

The size message sets the number of samples that fzero~ looks at when estimating the fundametal. In general, larger numbers are more accurate, but less efficient.
fzero~ does a new analysis every n number of samples.  The default is 256. NB: If this value is set to smaller than the current signal vector size, then the object outputs once every vector.
